`mount`: list or mount filesystems.

## Synopsis

<strong>mount</strong>\
<strong>mount</strong> <em>source dir</em>

## Description

With no arguments, <strong>mount</strong> lists what is mounted, sorted by path, one a line:

```text
\fIsource\fR on \fIpath\fR type \fItype\fR
```

The types are <strong>hfs</strong> (a disk), <strong>tmpfs</strong> (a filesystem in memory) and <strong>devfs</strong>.

With two arguments, <strong>mount</strong> mounts <em>source</em> on <em>dir</em>. <em>source</em> is a disk's bus address (its slot path, as <strong>sata:1</strong>, or its id, <strong>id:</strong><em>uuid</em><strong>;</strong> see <strong>lsdev</strong>(1)), which must be a storage device in hfs mode; or <strong>tmpfs</strong> for a new, empty filesystem in memory; or <strong>devfs</strong> for the device files. <em>dir</em> need not exist: a mount point shows up as a directory.

The kernel mounts the boot disk on <em>/</em>, devfs on <em>/dev</em>, a tmpfs on <em>/tmp</em>, and every other hfs disk on the bus under <em>/mnt</em> (<em>/mnt/sata/1</em> for <strong>sata:1</strong>) by itself, as disks come and go.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 with the wrong number of arguments, or if the mount failed (something is mounted there already: busy; not a storage device: no such device; a raw disk: invalid argument).

## Examples

```text
mount sata:2 /mnt/backup
mount tmpfs /scratch
```

## Notes

There are no options and no <em>/etc/fstab</em>; a filesystem type cannot be given apart from the source.

## See also

<strong>umount</strong>(1), <strong>df</strong>(1), <strong>lsdev</strong>(1)
